key_insight: LLMSurgeon formalizes "Data Mixture Surgery": from only text produced by a target LLM, it can estimate the domain-level composition of the model's pretraining corpus under a predefined taxonomy, revealing the model's "digital DNA."
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of transparency in LLM pretraining mixtures by enabling post-hoc estimation of domain proportions without access to the original training data or training logs.
method: Collect representative generations from the target LLM as probe data under controlled prompts.
Score or classify generated text against domain-specific reference models or classifiers to obtain per-sample domain signals.
Aggregate signals with a mixture-estimation algorithm (e.g., calibrated weighting / probabilistic EM-style inference) to recover domain-level proportions under the taxonomy.
impact: Enables practitioners and auditors to diagnose dataset composition, explain model behaviors or biases, and inform safer deployment, dataset curation, and regulatory compliance efforts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: probe generation → domain scoring/classifiers → mixture estimation
Pie chart or stacked bar showing inferred domain proportions (the recovered mixture)
Heatmap/confusion matrix showing classifier calibration and per-domain attribution uncertainty
Example snippets mapped to domains to illustrate how generated text signals provenance
paper_title: LLMSurgeon: Diagnosing Data Mixture of Large Language Models
paper_authors: Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xiaohan Zhao, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Liu
